destination.name: Litchfield National Park
destination.tagline: Waterfalls, swimming holes and giant termite mounds about an hour south of Darwin.
destination.description: Litchfield National Park covers about 1,500 square kilometres of the Tabletop Range south of Darwin. Spring-fed falls tumble off the sandstone plateau into plunge pools, and Buley Rockhole's cascades, the magnetic termite mounds and the sandstone pillars of the Lost City are all within a short drive of each other. The northern end is reached on sealed roads; the south needs a 4WD.
whyVisit: Swim beneath Wangi Falls in the Dry

goodToKnow.title: Parks pass required
goodToKnow.detail: Visitors need an NT Parks Visitor Pass: $10 adult per day, $20 for three days, $5 child. NT residents are exempt.

goodToKnow.title: Wet-season swimming limits
goodToKnow.detail: Wangi Falls swimming is closed in the wet season, typically October to March, and some areas close for flooding. Check before you go.

goodToKnow.title: Be crocwise
goodToKnow.detail: Swim only where signed safe; saltwater crocodiles can be in unsigned waters. The pool at Tolmer Falls is closed to swimmers.

destination.bestTimeBlurb: The Dry season, {months}, is the time for swimming and for reaching the 4WD tracks; in the Wet some areas flood and Wangi Falls closes to swimmers.
